function: Catalyzes endohydrolysis of 1,4-beta-D-glucosidic linkages in xyloglucan with retention of the beta-configuration of the glycosyl residues. Specific for xyloglucan and does not hydrolyze other cell wall components (PubMed:15094064, PubMed:22496365, PubMed:9884411). As an hydrolase for cell wall degradation, xgeA contributes to virulence, enabling to penetrate and utilize plant cell walls nutritionally (PubMed:22496365).

function: Catalyzes endohydrolysis of 1,4-beta-D-glucosidic linkages in xyloglucan with retention of the beta-configuration of the glycosyl residues (PubMed:28710128). Critical virulence factor for establishing infection in host plant that acts as an early cell death-inducing protein (CDIP) (PubMed:28710128). Induces cell death in dicot plants such as N.benthamiana, tomato and bean (Phaseolus vulgaris), but not in monocot plants, including maize and wheat (PubMed:28710128). The induction of necrosis does not depend on the glycosyl hydrolase activity (PubMed:28710128). The cell death-promoting signal is mediated by the host leucine-rich repeat receptor-like kinases BAK1 and SOBIR1 (PubMed:28710128). XYG1 is also recognized by the plant immune system and triggers pattern-triggered immunity (PTI) which induces systemic resistance (PubMed:28710128).
